question: Two laboratories report different 28-day concrete compressive strengths for the same cement trial, but one used a different specimen geometry and end-bearing preparation; what evidence must an agent reconcile before attributing the difference to cement quality?
category: Strength testing specimen geometry and loading boundary
scenario: Cross-laboratory comparison of cube versus cylinder geometry and capped versus ground bearing faces
evidence_required: Applicable test-method designation and edition for each laboratory, specimen type and exact dimensions
Specimen identification, casting and curing history, measured dimensions, end-face preparation and machine platen alignment
Raw failure loads, calculated stress, loading rate, machine calibration and replicate scatter
answer_and_decision_guide: Do not directly equate cube and cylinder strengths or apply an assumed universal conversion factor. Recalculate each result using its measured loaded area and applicable test method; check end-face preparation, loading alignment, failure mode and replicate dispersion. Compare only method-compatible specimens, or commission a documented paired-method study under competent laboratory supervision before assigning a cement-quality effect. No compliance or process adjustment follows from unharmonized values.
source_provenance: Seller-maintained contextual reading, not a validated test standard; independently confirm method edition, equipment and applicability.
free_first_decision: Use original test reports and applicable method first. No paid reference package is needed if the laboratory can reconcile geometry and loading records.

conditional_paid_check.authorization: Only after identifying an exact relevant listed file, verifying edition, rights, price and explicit buyer permission; never initiate payment.

model_limitations: No access to original machine traces, specimens, standards or laboratory calibration; cannot certify a result or assert a universal geometry conversion.
